extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants (SEC filers), CFOs, SEC reporting teams, auditors, sustainability/ESG reporting leads, and legal/compliance advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and presenting the climate-related disclosures required by the SEC final rule (Regulation S-X Article 14 and related SEC filing disclosures), including financial-statement footnote items, GHG metrics, governance, strategy, risk management, targets, and assurance/internal controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement disclosures (Regulation S-X, Article 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose in the footnotes to the financial statements: (1) specified financial statement effects of severe weather events and other natural conditions, (2) certain carbon offsets and renewable energy certificates (RECs), and (3) material impacts on financial estimates and assumptions that are due to severe weather events and other natural conditions or disclosed climate-related targets or transition plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all registrants (except asset-backed issuers), including EGCs, SRCs, and foreign private issuers; disclosures should be prepared consistent with the scope of consolidated financial statements and same accounting principles; supplement disclosures with contextual information necessary for investors (significant inputs, assumptions, judgments, policy decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement effects of severe weather and other natural conditions (income statement and balance sheet effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure is bifurcated into: (1) income statement effects — expenditures expensed as incurred and losses (e.g., restore operations, relocate assets, retire or repair assets, recognize impairment loss, otherwise respond) and (2) balance sheet effects — capitalized costs and charges (e.g., restore, retire, replace or repair, recognize impairment charge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All severe weather events or other natural conditions are subject to the requirement regardless of causation by climate change; registrants must develop accounting policies and apply judgement to determine what qualifies; provide separate statement of amounts recognized in each financial statement line item affected and disclose recoveries separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution — 'significant contributing factor' rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts included should be transactions recorded in a registrant’s books during the fiscal year; registrants are not required to allocate amounts based on an estimate of the extent to which effects were due to the event. If a severe weather event was a 'significant contributing factor' to recognition of expenditures, losses, capitalized costs, charges, or recoveries, include the entire amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule does not define 'significant'; registrants should develop an accounting policy for determining significance and consider ASC guidance (e.g., ASC 280, ASC 323, ASC 810, ASC 820) and relevant interpretations when doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure thresholds for income statement effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure required in notes if aggregate income statement effects equal or exceed the greater of 1% of the absolute value of pretax income (loss) or $100,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine aggregate amounts before considering recoveries (such as insurance); if threshold met, separately state amounts by affected financial statement line item and state recoveries recognized in each affected line item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure thresholds for balance sheet effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure required in notes if aggregate balance sheet effects equal or exceed the greater of 1% of the absolute value of stockholders’ equity (or deficit) or $500,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same aggregation/presentation rules as income statement effects; registrants need processes, procedures, and internal controls to identify and aggregate these amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon offsets and RECs financial statement disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: When use of carbon offsets or RECs is a material component of a registrant’s plan to achieve a disclosed climate-related target or goal, the registrant must disclose: the aggregate amount expensed, capitalized, and losses incurred during the fiscal year; the beginning and ending balances of amounts capitalized; the income statement and balance sheet line item(s) in which amounts are expensed or capitalized or losses are recognized; and the accounting policy for carbon offsets or RECs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carbon offsets = 'an emissions reduction, removal, or avoidance of [GHGs] in a manner calculated and traced for the purpose of offsetting an entity’s GHG emissions.' A REC = 'a credit or certificate representing each megawatt-hour (1 MWh) of renewable electricity generated and delivered to a power grid.' These disclosures anchor outside-the-statement disclosures to those within audited financial statements; disclosures are required only if use of offsets/RECs is a material component of achieving a disclosed material target/goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimates and assumptions affected by climate considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are required to disclose whether severe weather events, other natural conditions, or any disclosed climate-related targets or transition plans have materially affected estimates and assumptions reflected in the financial statements, and if so, provide a qualitative explanation of the impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No disclosure is required if registrant concludes estimates/assumptions were not materially affected; emphasizes need for clear communication between finance/accounting and those overseeing climate targets/transition plans (e.g., asset retirements affecting useful lives).

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG emission metrics required (Scope 1 and Scope 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large accelerated filers and accelerated filers (other than SRCs and EGCs) must disclose material Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 GHG emissions (gross emissions before offsets) for each category on the basis of metric tons of CO2e; separately disclose each constituent GHG that is individually material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope 1 = direct GHG emissions from operations owned or controlled; Scope 2 = indirect emissions from generation of purchased or acquired electricity, steam, heat, or cooling consumed by operations owned or controlled; assurance over GHG disclosures is required (phased in).

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality assessment for GHG emission disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must determine whether Scope 1 or Scope 2 emissions are material; materiality is not determined solely by absolute amount but whether a reasonable investor would consider the information important in deciding how to vote or invest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider regulatory exposure, potential penalties, relevance to transition plans/targets and progress; registrant may disclose only the emissions categories it determines are material (e.g., Scope 1 material but Scope 2 not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods and assumptions for GHG calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must provide a brief description of the protocol or standard used to report GHG emissions, including calculation approach, type and source of emission factors, and any tools used to calculate GHG emissions; must disclose Scope 2 method (location-based or market-based) and whether RECs factored into gross emissions calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not required to include lengthy numeric emission factor tables; may make reasonable estimates but must disclose assumptions underlying and reasons for estimates. Final rule refers to frameworks such as the GHG Protocol, EPA regulations, and ISO standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational and operational boundaries for GHG disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must describe the organizational boundaries used to calculate GHG emissions, the method used to determine such boundaries, and briefly explain any material differences between those boundaries and the scope of entities and operations included in consolidated financial statements. Also discuss operational boundaries, including categorization of emissions and emission sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule does not mandate a specific approach; registrants may leverage existing voluntary reporting boundaries (e.g., operational control) but must describe material differences if the scope differs from consolidated financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance disclosures (board and management oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose how their board of directors oversees assessment and management of climate-related risks: the specific board committee(s) or subcommittee(s) responsible, processes by which board committees are informed of climate-related risks, and whether/how committees oversee progress toward disclosed targets/goals. Management disclosures (specific executives/committees, relevant expertise, processes, and reporting to the board) are required only if they apply to oversight of material risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose any climate-related risks overseen by the board; materiality is not considered for matters overseen by the board because such matters are generally expected to be material. Provide 'in such detail as necessary to fully describe the nature of the expertise.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy disclosures — description of material climate-related risks and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must describe any climate-related risks that have had or are reasonably likely to have a material effect on business strategy, results of operations, or financial condition, and whether risks are expected to manifest in the short term (next 12 months) and/or long term (beyond 12 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both physical risks (acute and chronic) and transition risks; required elements include nature of risk, geographic location, nature of properties/processes subject to risk, whether risk relates to regulatory/technological/market/other factors, and the impact of those factors on the registrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures by type of climate risk (physical vs transition)
rubrics_metrics.description: For physical risks: indicate whether acute or chronic, geographic location, and nature of properties/processes subject to risk. For transition risks: indicate whether risk is related to regulatory, technological, market (e.g., changing consumer or investor preferences), or other transition-related factors and the impact on the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For all material climate-related risks, disclose the actual or potential material impacts to strategy, business model, and outlook, including impacts to operations, products/services, suppliers/contract counterparties, transition activities, and R&D expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on strategy, financial planning, and capital allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose how climate-related risks affect strategy, financial planning, and capital allocation, including whether and how risks influence operations, product/service offerings, suppliers/purchasers, transition activities, and research and development spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose separately for short-term and long-term horizons and include known or reasonably available information about impacts on suppliers/purchasers/counterparties to material contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management processes for material climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must describe the processes they use to identify, assess, and manage material climate-related risks and whether and how those processes are integrated into the registrant’s overall risk management framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include procedures for monitoring, prioritization, and escalation; describe how climate-related risks are assessed and how that assessment informs operational or strategic decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targets and goals disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose material climate-related targets and goals, including the target metrics, time frames, baselines, interim targets, scope (e.g., organizational/operational boundaries), related actions, and progress toward achieving the targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the target materially affected or is reasonably likely to materially affect business, results, or financial condition, registrant must disclose it; if scenario analysis is used and results yield material impacts, disclosure of scenario analysis is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit, assurance, and internal control requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statement disclosures will be subject to existing financial statement audit requirements and management’s internal control over financial reporting (ICFR); assurance requirements for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions will be phased in for applicable registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should prepare for assurance by understanding assurance requirements, developing plans to provide sufficient support, and consider internal controls and documentation necessary to support audit and assurance engagements. Voluntary assurance obtained before requirement triggers additional disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation and presentation requirements in disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosures are required, registrants must aggregate amounts recorded in their books during the fiscal year and separately state amounts by affected financial statement line item. Registrants must determine aggregated amounts before considering recoveries and separately state recoveries recognized in each affected line item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contextual information to help investors understand preparation methods; ensure processes and controls exist to identify, aggregate, and disclose appropriate amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reasonable estimates and disclosure of underlying assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may make reasonable estimates in calculating GHG emissions or other climate-related quantitative information, but must disclose the assumptions underlying, and reasons for using, the estimates to help investors understand calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule gives domestic registrants additional time to provide annual GHG emission disclosures, which may reduce circumstances requiring estimation for parts of the reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional/voluntary disclosures (Scope 3, intensity measures, voluntary assurance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule does not require Scope 3 GHG emissions or GHG intensity measures, but registrants may voluntarily provide such information. Voluntary assurance on Scope 1 and Scope 2 may be obtained but triggers additional disclosure obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrants voluntarily obtain assurance on emissions disclosed in an SEC filing, they must provide disclosures discussed in the Voluntary GHG Emission Assurance Considerations section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to recognized frameworks and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: While the final rule does not mandate a specific calculation method, it refers to certain frameworks (e.g., the GHG Protocol corporate standard, EPA regulations, applicable ISO standards) that registrants may use for GHG accounting and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies that already report voluntarily under these frameworks may leverage existing information but must describe any material differences in boundaries or methods relative to consolidated financial statements and satisfy SEC disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation considerations and recommended preparatory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful implementation starts with planning: establish/refine management responsibilities and board oversight, inventory current climate disclosure and data, identify disclosure and control gaps, assess reporting and data management needs, prepare for assurance, develop and execute an action plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educate management, employees, and board; define roles; incorporate oversight responsibilities into charters; integrate action plan with other climate reporting requirements (e.g., CSRD); begin executing and adapt for future developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of examples and illustrative disclosure language
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance provides concrete examples (e.g., Example 1 — financial statement effects from wildfire/hurricane; Example 2 — carbon offsets and RECs accounting) illustrating calculation, threshold testing, and sample note disclosure formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples as templates for preparing contextual disclosures, note X formatting, and calculations; when thresholds are met, registrants should consider how to present affected line items and recoveries clearly for investors.
